title: Capcom is preparing for a 'future where we create games together with AI'
source_used: IGN (own article citing Japanese outlet GameBiz); The Verge also read, which rests on IGN
key_facts: On 2 Oct 2026 Capcom held its Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026; programmer Satoshi Ishida presented the REX project, a multi-step upgrade of the RE Engine.
Ishida named three problems: games so large that simple tasks take too long, bigger teams needing an easier engine, and the need to integrate AI into development workflows.
Capcom's long-term goal is to turn the RE Engine into an 'AI-generation game engine' and reach 'a future where we create games together with AI'.
REX unifies the engine under a very common programming language so both people and AI can work with it; some parts will be open-sourced for AI training.
Capcom said at its March 2026 shareholders meeting that it will not put AI-generated assets into its games but will use AI to improve development efficiency.
IGN's account rests on a report by Japanese outlet GameBiz; The Verge cites IGN's translation.
quote_evidence: On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called 'Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.'
Capcom's goal is to build a future where it "creates games together with AI"
"We will not implement assets generated by AI into our games." Capcom said in a March 2026 shareholders meeting.
why_it_matters_hint: A major Japanese publisher is rebuilding its engine around AI-assisted development while keeping its pledge not to ship AI-generated art.
notes: Chain: The Verge cites IGN, IGN cites GameBiz (Japanese). Source credited as IGN, citing GameBiz. Conference was 2 Oct, one day before the scan window.
